review_comments: I wonder if we could keep the check that the error message mentions `my_remote_cluster` (if that's the case) maybe without requiring all other stuff to match.

Since I'm not able to reproduce the failure, I'm hesitant to do that. We don't control what error messages come from the underlying transport layer, so testing for that doesn't test for anything we can change. The error message will be whatever the transport layer decides it wants it to be depending on what exact sequence of transport issues happened (and there can be many different errors from disconnected clusters). The key point of this test is that it reports some sort of disconnected/transport error rather than an ESQL verification exception which is what it was doing before [Pawan's fix](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/119750).
